title: Dispatch: implement the offline discovery stage harness (attempt 1)
description:
WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.10.1`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.10.1`
(cut from parent branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.10`, which is `origin/main` @ fbd3efd).

Parent bead `eshyra-o9bd.19.10` (Transition W8) carries the authority, scope,
prohibitions, and acceptance criteria. Read it with `bd show` first. The
governing design is
`docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md`
sections 6, 7, 8.2, 11, 12.1, 13.1, 13.2, 13.3; ADR 0020 controls. Read
sections 6, 7, 8.2, 12.1, 13 yourself before writing code — this plan
summarises them but the document is the authority and wins on any conflict.

The supervisor has already surveyed the substrate. What follows is the
pre-planning, not a licence to skip verification: check every claim marked
[VERIFY] against the tree before you rely on it.

====================================================================
A. WHAT EXISTS ALREADY (verified by the supervisor at fbd3efd)
====================================================================

W7 landed the fixture corpus:
- `packages/core/test/diagnostics/fixtureContract.ts` — types + validator.
  Key exported types: `DiagnosticFixture`, `FixtureExecution`, `RouteClass`
  (the nine section-6.2 labels), `DiagnosticTarget` (`rules-record` |
  `adventure-entity` | `absent-rules-record`), `DiagnosticSelector`,
  `RetainedFact`, `TypedRelationshipExpectation`, `RouteExpectation`,
  `AmbiguityExpectation`, `CampaignRuleCase`, `CapabilityExpectation`,
  `OracleSignal`, `ExplicitNone`.
- `packages/core/test/diagnostics/probes/p01..p12*.ts` and
  `packages/core/test/diagnostics/index.ts` exporting `DIAGNOSTIC_FIXTURES`.
- `packages/core/test/diagnosticFixtureCorpus.test.ts` validates the fixtures
  against the real pack and module. Do not weaken it, and do not edit the
  fixtures to make the harness pass. If a fixture expectation is genuinely
  wrong, stop and file a bead against `eshyra-o9bd.19.9` instead.

Canonical target reference strings (match the private `targetReference()` in
`fixtureContract.ts`): rules-record and absent-rules-record use `recordKey`;
adventure-entity uses `${moduleId}#${entityKind}:${entityId}`. Reuse exactly
this convention for candidate keys so measurements line up.

Real substrate you MUST use (no fixture copies of packs):
- `packages/core/src/rules/stack.ts` — `resolveRulesStack`,
  `ResolvedRulesStack` (`recordsByKey`, `recordsByKind` with `byKey`/`byName`),
  `RulesStackRecordEntry` (`record`, `pack`, `license`, `overrideChain`),
  and `normalizeRulesRecordName`.
- `packages/core/src/state/campaignRecordLookup.ts` —
  `resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack(db, resolver)`, `CampaignRulesPackResolver`.
- `packages/core/src/rules/bundledSrdPack.ts` — `getBundledDnd5eSrdPack()`
  loads the generated pack (1812 records) from `packages/core/data`.
- `packages/core/src/rules/conditionRelations.ts` —
  `CONDITION_RELATION_VALUES` (the closed relation vocabulary).
- `packages/core/src/state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts` —
  `assertMagicItemOperationReady(record, variantId, input)`,
  `ItemOperationReadinessInput`, `ItemExecutionReadinessError`.
- `packages/core/test/support/db.ts` — `bareDb()`, `freshDbWithSession()`.
- `packages/core/test/support/cursedAttunementAddon.ts` —
  `installCursedAttunementAddon(db, at)` returns the resolver and writes the
  campaign binding; P11 needs it.
- `packages/core/src/adventure/` — module loading (`loadAdventureModuleFromDir`
  via `src/internal.ts`) and `adventure/references.ts`.

Verified pack facts you may rely on (re-check if surprised):
- `rule:cover`, `rule:opportunity-attacks`, `rule:concentration` carry only
  `data.text` — no typed mechanics, so they are reachable only by cue.
- `condition:incapacitated` has `data.effects` and `data.mechanics`.
- `mechanics.conditions` entries carry `{condition: "<name>", relation: "<rel>"}`
  where `condition` is the bare name (e.g. `"incapacitated"`), NOT the record
  key. 136 records carry `mechanics.conditions`; 21 name `incapacitated`.
- Typed link fields present in the pack: `data.source` (197),
  `data.mechanics.conditions` (136), `data.tableRefs` (73),
  `data.progressionTableRef` (12), `data.parentClass` (12),
  `data.spellTableRefs` (4), `data.statBlockRefs` (2).
- `feature:fighter:action-surge` has `data.source === 'class:fighter'`.
- `action:dodge` has `mechanics.conditions = [{condition:'incapacitated',
  relation:'exclusion'}]`.
- `magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3` readiness: C1 `economies/use` green, C2
  `effects` engine-pending (F8). Operation `hit-target`.
- `magic-item:cube-of-force` readiness: `operations/press-face-1` is
  engine-pending (F5), so preflight for `press-face-1` must be BLOCKED.
- Only 3 records carry `mechanics.ambiguities`.

====================================================================
B. WHERE THE CODE GOES
====================================================================

Production module tree, exported ONLY through `@eshyra/core/internal`
(`packages/core/src/internal.ts`), never through `src/index.ts`:

  packages/core/src/discovery/
    types.ts              stage/trace/packet/route types
    signals.ts            stage 1
    candidates.ts         stage 2
    expansion.ts          stage 3
    campaignRuleSeam.ts   stage 4 seam (interface + null implementation)
    dedup.ts              stage 5
    retention.ts          stage 6
    packet.ts             stage 7
    harness.ts            runDiscoveryStages(): orchestrates 1-7, returns trace
    measurements.ts       M1-M9

Rationale for `src/` rather than `test/`: AGENTS.md's convention is that new
core symbols default to the `/internal` subpath, which exists for
co-developed in-repo callers; W9 (`eshyra-o9bd.19.11`) has to wire this same
pipeline into the orchestrator seam, and a test-only home would force a move.
This stays experiment-only in the sense the bead requires: NOTHING in
`src/orchestrator`, `src/state`, `src/session`, or the CLI may import it. Add a
test that asserts that (grep-style guard, in the same spirit as
`packages/core/test/nodeRuntimePolicy.test.ts`).

Tests:
  packages/core/test/discovery/discoverySignals.test.ts
  packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryStages.test.ts
  packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryProbes.test.ts
  packages/core/test/discovery/support/scenario.ts        fixture -> harness input
  packages/core/test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts  the jhpt stub

====================================================================
C. THE PIPELINE
====================================================================

Stages, in order (design section 12.1):
  signals -> candidates -> typed expansion -> campaign-rule/ruling join
  -> dedup -> priority/retention -> context packet

EVERY stage returns its own trace object, and `runDiscoveryStages` returns
`{ signals, candidates, expansion, ruleJoin, dedup, retention, packet }` plus a
flat `stageOrder` list. No stage may mutate a prior stage's trace. Nothing is
persisted anywhere: no DB writes, no files, no artifact emission. The harness
takes a `Db` ONLY to resolve the campaign rules binding through
`resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack`; it must never write to it.

Every stage trace records, at minimum: inputs consumed, outputs produced,
and losses (with a reason). A stage that produced nothing and recorded no
loss must be reported as `failed-to-run`, not as passing (design 13.3).

--- Stage 1: signals (`signals.ts`) ---

Input: `DiscoveryScenario`:
  {
    playerInput: string,
    actingCharacterId?: string,
    stateFields: Record<string, unknown>,   // the fixture's campaignState
    adventure?: { moduleId, locationId?, encounterId?, module: AdventureModule },
    itemInstances?: readonly { instanceId, recordKey, variantId? }[],
    oracleSignals?: readonly InjectedSignal[],   // for stage-independent tests
  }

Output signals, each `{ signalId, kind, evidence, proposes }` where `evidence`
names the exact input field or text span it came from.

Signal kinds and their extractors:
1. `state-ref`: walk `stateFields` (recursively, recording the JSON path of
   every value visited). Any string value matching `^<kind>:<slug>$` where
   `<kind>` is a member of `RULES_RECORD_KINDS` becomes a state-ref signal
   proposing that record key. Also resolve the declared `itemInstances`
   bindings (instanceId -> recordKey) when a state field's value equals a
   known instanceId. Record the binding in the trace as a scenario-state
   binding so it is never hidden.
   `conditions: ['condition:incapacitated']` and
   `activeEffects: [{kind:'concentration', source:'spell:hold-person'}]`
   are both covered by the generic walk.
2. `adventure-ref`: from `scenario.adventure`, propose the selected
   location and encounter entity targets, and every `rulesRef` carried by the
   selected encounter's creature entries and the selected location.
3. `name-mention`: normalize `playerInput` with `normalizeRulesRecordName`,
   tokenize, and look up token n-grams (up to the longest indexed record name,
   bounded) against each kind's `byName` index. A hit where the name maps to
   exactly ONE entry proposes that record key. A hit where the name maps to
   several entries is recorded as an `ambiguous-name` observation (not a
   candidate) with every colliding key listed — that mirrors the `lookup.ts`
   exact/ambiguous contract and must never be resolved by picking one.
4. `situation-cue`: a small, explicit, declared cue table (see D below).
5. `capability-preflight`: when the scenario names an `operationId` together
   with an item record (directly or through an `itemInstances` binding),
   propose that record with the operation id attached.
6. `auditor-missing-target`: define the signal kind for completeness, but no
   extractor is required — no fixture exercises it. Say so in the module doc.

MANDATORY: any `stateFields` leaf the signals stage did NOT consume must be
reported in the trace as `unconsumedStateFields` (path + value shape). Silently
ignoring scenario state is exactly the "recognising nothing looks green"
failure the design forbids.

`oracleSignals` are merged in, each flagged `oracleSupplied: true` with the
label the caller supplied, and the stage trace exposes
`oracleSuppliedSignalLabels` so downstream reporting can label the probe.

--- Stage 2: candidates (`candidates.ts`) ---

Resolve every signal's proposed target against the REAL resolved stack
(`ResolvedRulesStack.recordsByKey`) and, for adventure entities, against the
loaded module. Produce `DiscoveryCandidate`:
  { candidateKey, targetKind: 'rules-record'|'adventure-entity',
    entry?: RulesStackRecordEntry, adventureEntity?: {...},
    routes: DiscoveryRoute[] }
`DiscoveryRoute` = { routeClass: RouteClass, trigger: string,
  evidence: Record<string, unknown>, signalId: string }.

A proposed target that does not resolve is a recorded loss
(`unresolved-target`), never a silent drop.

--- Stage 3: typed expansion (`expansion.ts`) ---

ONE hop, only over links the pack already types. Two directions, because the
fixtures require both:
- forward: from a candidate record, follow `data.source`, `data.parentClass`,
  `data.tableRefs`, `data.progressionTableRef`, `data.spellTableRefs`,
  `data.statBlockRefs`, and `data.mechanics.conditions` (relation value from
  `CONDITION_RELATION_VALUES`; the `condition` field is a bare NAME and must be
  resolved to a `condition:*` record key through the stack's condition-kind
  `byName` index, not by string-concatenating a key).
- reverse: records whose typed link points AT a candidate. Build the reverse
  index once per stack resolution from the same closed field list.

Every traversal is emitted as
`{ sourceRecordKey, linkField, relation, targetRecordKey }` matching
`TypedRelationshipExpectation` exactly, so M4 can compare directly. `linkField`
strings must match the fixture's declared form (P5 declares
`'data.mechanics.conditions'`); for fields with no relation value use the field
name as the relation (state the convention in the module doc and keep it
consistent). BOTH endpoints of an emitted traversal gain a `typed-relationship`
route: this is what P6 (`feature:fighter:action-surge` gains the route from its
own outgoing `data.source` link) and P5 (`condition:incapacitated` gains it from
the inbound `action:dodge` exclusion link) require. The endpoint that was not
already a candidate becomes a NEW candidate. Cap the expansion at one hop; new
candidates from expansion are never themselves expanded.

--- Stage 4: campaign-rule/ruling join (`campaignRuleSeam.ts`) ---

Define the narrow READ interface required by design 8.2, and nothing more:

  export interface CampaignRuleReadSeam {
    activeRulesAtPosition(query: {
      campaignPosition?: string;
      candidateRecordKeys: readonly string[];
    }): readonly ActiveCampaignRuleProjection[];
    activeRulingsForAmbiguities(
      ambiguityIds: readonly string[],
    ): readonly ActiveCampaignRulingProjection[];
  }

`ActiveCampaignRuleProjection` carries: `ruleIdentity`, `ruleKind`
('house-rule'|'ruling'), `status`, `origin`, `provenance`, `effectivePosition`,
`supersededBy` (null when none), `scope`, and `governingRecordKeys` (design
8.3 A1) and/or `ambiguityId`. `ActiveCampaignRulingProjection` additionally
carries `ambiguityId` and `selectedInterpretationId`.

Ship a `NULL_CAMPAIGN_RULE_SEAM` in `src` that returns empty arrays for both
methods, and document that `eshyra-jhpt` owns the real implementation (W11
consumes it). NO rule/ruling schema, store, resolver, lifecycle, persistence,
or supersession logic may be implemented here — the seam only reads.

The join stage: request active rules for the current candidate key set and
active rulings for every ambiguity id discovered on candidate records
(`data.mechanics.ambiguities[].id`). For each returned projection, attach a
`campaign-rule` or `campaign-ruling` route to the candidate(s) it governs, and
record the pairing (`ruleIdentity` -> governing candidate key) for M5. A
projection that names no resolvable governing candidate is recorded as an
`unplaced-rule` loss — never dropped silently. A discovered ambiguity with no
active ruling stays `unresolved` in the trace (design 8.2 R7); discovery must
NEVER resolve an ambiguity itself.

The test-side stub lives in
`packages/core/test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts`: an explicit,
clearly-labelled table keyed by `${probeId}/${executionId}`, with entries only
for the two executions whose fixtures declare active campaign-rule state and
oracle signals (P7 `with-active-ruling`, P10 `default`). Every projection it
returns is flagged oracle-supplied, and any probe consuming it is reported
with the join stage labelled `oracle-supplied`.

--- Stage 5: dedup (`dedup.ts`) ---

Merge by canonical candidate key. Preserve EVERY route and EVERY traversal
reason. The trace records `routeCountBeforeDedup`, `routeCountAfterDedup` per
candidate and in total; any decrease is a hard failure (throw), not a warning
(design 6.2, M3). Route identity for dedup purposes is
(routeClass, trigger, signalId) — two genuinely identical route records may
collapse, but the trace must show that the collapse was of identical records.

--- Stage 6: priority and retention (`retention.ts`) ---

Bands (design 6.3):
  must-consider: direct-state-ref, direct-adventure-ref,
                 explicit-name-or-alias, campaign-rule, campaign-ruling,
                 capability-preflight
  related:       typed-relationship
  exploratory:   situation-cue, auditor-missing-target
A candidate's band is the strongest band any of its routes earns.

IMPORTANT: `situation-cue` is exploratory by section 6.3, and P1, P2 and P5's
`rule:concentration` are must-include TARGETS reached ONLY by cue. Retention
must therefore be generous enough that exploratory candidates for those probes
survive; a must-include target that is dropped by the budget is an M1/M2
failure the probe reports, not something to paper over by reclassifying the
band. Do NOT move `situation-cue` into must-consider — the bands come from the
design.

Ranking within a band: route count descending, then canonical key ascending.
Deterministic and simple only — no ranker, no scoring model, no embeddings.

Budget: `{ maxCandidates, maxPacketBytes }` with documented defaults chosen so
that no probe drops a must-include target. Must-consider candidates are NEVER
dropped: if the must-consider set alone exceeds the budget, emit an
`overflow` record naming every dropped candidate with its full route list and
mark the run `overflowed: true` — the probe runner MUST fail such a probe.
Related and exploratory drops are permitted and each records its reason.

--- Stage 7: context packet (`packet.ts`) ---

For each retained candidate emit the design 7.1 fields:
  canonical identity (key, kind, name);
  provenance (`provenance.sourceRef`, `provenance.locator`, `source` label,
    license identity from the stack entry);
  source prose (`description`, `text`, the relevant `actions[i].text`,
    `higherLevels`, ... — carry the record's prose fields verbatim; do not
    truncate a required retained fact out of the packet);
  every route with its trigger detail;
  every traversal that produced the candidate;
  known source ambiguity (`id`, `question`, `interpretations[].id`,
    `canonicalResolution`) — always surfaced, resolved or not;
  applicable campaign rule/ruling with identity, scope, provenance,
    supersession status, placed beside the governing material;
  capability status (see E) with inputs, exclusions, revision, and residual
    interpretation;
  projection-limit notes (see F).

Packet prohibitions (design 7.3) — enforce each with a test:
- never present a route-free record as authoritative (a candidate with zero
  routes is a bug: throw);
- never present a typed projection as a capability;
- never turn "no capability bound" into "no mechanics";
- never drop a must-consider candidate silently;
- never launder known-false provenance (P12);
- never claim the model used anything.

====================================================================
D. THE SITUATION-CUE TABLE
====================================================================

Section 6.2 says this class has no substrate today and that a cue "matches a
fixture-declared cue". The fixtures do not carry a cue field, so the harness
owns a small, explicit, DECLARED cue table. Rules for it:
- each entry is `{ cueId, description, derivationInputs, proposes: recordKey[],
  match(scenario): CueMatch | undefined }`;
- matching keys off STRUCTURED scenario state (and, where unavoidable, a
  narrowly documented text predicate), NEVER off a probe id, fixture identity,
  or the expected outputs. A cue that reads the fixture's expectations is a
  defect, not a shortcut;
- every match records the cue id, the exact derivation input, and the proposed
  record — that is the section 6.2 "recorded evidence" column;
- the table's module doc states plainly that it is a pilot cue set, that it is
  not a model of how rules become relevant, and that a cue's absence is
  evidence about the pilot rather than about the rules (section 6.4).

Three cues are needed by the corpus. Derive their exact match conditions from
the fixtures' campaignState yourself; the shapes are:
- geometry/obstacle cue: combat state carrying an obstacle description ->
  `rule:cover` (P1: `combat: {attacker, target, geometry: 'low wall between
  them'}`, and the player text deliberately never says "cover");
- movement-out-of-reach cue: a movement intent leaving melee reach ->
  `rule:opportunity-attacks` (P2);
- concentration-under-condition cue: an active `concentration` effect present
  together with condition state -> `rule:concentration` (P5).

Keep the obstacle vocabulary tiny, explicit, and documented (a short declared
noun list is fine); do not build a general text classifier.

====================================================================
E. CAPABILITY PREFLIGHT — SCOPE LIMIT, STATED HONESTLY
====================================================================

Only the magic-item readiness path has a real preflight in the tree today
(design 6.2 cites `assertMagicItemOperationReady`). Do this:

1. Extract, from `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts` (the block running
   roughly from `const mechanics = mechanicsFor(hit.record, variantId)` to the
   `assertMagicItemOperationReady(...)` call, near lines 1834-1908 [VERIFY the
   exact range]), a pure helper that derives `ItemOperationReadinessInput` from
   `(record, variantId, operationId)` — the operation lookup including the
   activate/deactivate state-machine fallback, `economyIds` from the
   operation's cost entries, `operationEffectIds`, `effectIds` (operation
   effects plus possible transition effects), `usesStateMachine`, and
   `usesSpellStore`. Call it from BOTH `itemState.ts` and the harness. This
   must be a pure, behaviour-preserving extraction: the existing item tests
   must pass unchanged, and you must not alter error types, messages, or
   ordering. If the extraction cannot be done cleanly, STOP and record why in
   the bead rather than forcing it.
2. The harness's preflight stage calls the extracted derivation plus the real
   `assertMagicItemOperationReady`, and reports
   `available` (no throw) or `blocked` (throws `ItemExecutionReadinessError`,
   carrying the message and the blocking clause ids as evidence), along with
   the contract revision (`derived-magic-item-clauses-v1`), the operation's
   declared inputs, and the clause-level exclusions.
   Expected: P8 `hit-target` -> available; P7 `press-face-1` -> blocked.
3. For every OTHER capability a fixture declares (`spell-upcast`,
   `concentration-lifecycle`), the packet records
   `not-evaluated-offline` naming the capability id and stating that
   contract-declared capability status is owned by W13
   (`eshyra-olc5.6`) and by M10, which is a Phase 2 measurement. Do NOT
   fabricate an `implemented` status, and do NOT build a capability-contract
   registry — that is W13's, not yours. The probe report shows the fixture's
   expectation beside the harness's `not-evaluated-offline` finding as an
   explicit, visible gap. M1-M9 are the Phase 1 gate; capability agreement
   is M10 and is out of Phase 1 scope.

====================================================================
F. PROJECTION-LIMIT NOTES
====================================================================

Design 7.2 requires the packet to disclose, in band, what a partial typed
projection omits. Implement a small, declared, deterministic set of detectors,
each carrying the evidence it fired on:
- a typed `saves[]` entry with no `damageOnSuccess`, while the record's prose
  contains a success-branch phrase -> note that the projection omits the
  success branch (P3 `creature:adult-black-dragon` action index 5);
- prose describing an area (a "<n>-foot radius/line/cone/cube/sphere" form)
  with no `mechanics.area` present -> note that no typed area exists
  (P3's 60-foot line, P4's 20-foot-radius sphere);
- a record carrying `executionReadiness` clauses that are not `green` -> note
  which clauses are engine-pending and which engines they name.
Keep the detector list short and documented; each must state what it does NOT
detect. A projection-limit note must never be emitted as a capability, and the
prose must be preserved verbatim beside it.

====================================================================
G. MEASUREMENTS M1-M9 (`measurements.ts`)
====================================================================

Computed per probe AND per stage from the returned trace, never persisted:
- M1 must-target retrieval: per must-include target, reached the packet or not.
- M2 loss stage: for each missed must-include target, the exact stage that lost
  it (signals | candidates | expansion | rule-join | dedup | retention |
  packet). Derive this by walking the stage traces, not by guessing.
- M3 preserved route count: routes per retained candidate after dedup vs the
  routes produced before dedup.
- M4 relationship expansion: for each `requiredRelationshipExpansion` entry,
  whether it fired, did not fire, or fired and was later dropped.
- M5 campaign-rule/ruling result: which rules/rulings were requested from the
  seam, which matched, which were placed beside their governing material.
- M6 mandatory-candidate retention: whether every must-consider candidate
  survived; an overflow record fails the probe.
- M7 packet size: bytes and candidate count, plus the recorded reason for each
  related/exploratory drop.
- M8 false authoritative inclusions: any `absent-rules-record`
  must-not-include target present in the packet, and any candidate whose
  provenance is known-false (P12's standing check).
- M9 missing source facts: for each `requiredRetainedFacts` entry with an
  `exactSubstring` or `typedPath`/`expectedValue`, whether it survived into the
  packet. Facts carrying only `statement` prose are NOT machine-checkable:
  report them explicitly as `prose-only-not-checkable`, and never count them as
  satisfied.

Independence rules (design 13.2) — enforce them structurally:
- these are separate fields on a per-probe result; there is no combined score,
  no percentage, no coverage/readiness/completeness figure anywhere in the
  code, the report, or the test names;
- the only permitted aggregate is a COUNT of probes passing;
- add a test asserting that the measurement result type has no aggregate score
  field and that the reporter emits none.

====================================================================
H. TESTS AND THE EVIDENCE THE BEAD REQUIRES
====================================================================

1. `discoverySignals.test.ts` — signal extraction ALONE, per fixture, with no
   downstream stage in the assertion path (design 12.1: a failure at one stage
   must never be hidden by success at another). Assert the expected signal
   kinds and their evidence for each probe, assert `unconsumedStateFields`
   reporting works, and assert the ambiguous-name observation path.
2. `discoveryStages.test.ts` — each stage boundary independently, driven by
   INJECTED inputs (oracle signals / synthetic candidates), covering:
   forward and reverse typed expansion including the exact P5 and P6
   traversals; dedup route preservation and the hard failure when a route
   would be lost; the retention bands and ranking order; a DELIBERATE
   must-consider overflow with a tiny budget, asserting the overflow record
   names every dropped candidate with its routes and that the run is marked
   failed; the packet's 7.3 prohibitions; projection-limit notes on
   `creature:adult-black-dragon` and `spell:fireball`; the preflight
   available/blocked results for `hit-target` and `press-face-1`; the seam
   returning nothing leaving a discovered ambiguity unresolved.
3. `discoveryProbes.test.ts` — every fixture, every execution, end to end
   through `runDiscoveryStages`, computing M1-M9 per probe per stage. Each
   probe asserts:
   - each stage ran (produced output or recorded a loss) — a stage with no
     candidates, no routes and no losses fails the probe as `failed-to-run`;
   - every expected route class from `expectedRouteClasses` is PRESENT on the
     named target (superset allowed; extras are reported in the trace, and a
     `campaign-rule`/`campaign-ruling` route appearing with no active rule
     state is a failure);
   - M1 reaches every must-include target; M6 has no overflow; M8 finds no
     false authoritative inclusion; M9 finds no missing machine-checkable fact;
     M4 fires every declared traversal;
   - the probe result carries `oracleSupplied` labels naming every stage that
     was handed its answer (the two jhpt executions, and any scenario-state
     binding used), so a probe that passed on an oracle is reported as such.
4. `discoveryBoundary.test.ts` (or fold into the stages test) — assert no
   module under `src/orchestrator`, `src/state`, `src/session`, `src/campaign`,
   `src/memory`, or `packages/cli` imports `src/discovery`, and that
   `src/index.ts` does not export it.

The probe test must PRINT nothing that looks like a coverage figure. Report
per-probe results as structured data in assertions.

====================================================================
I. PROHIBITIONS (from the parent bead and ADR 0020) — read them again
====================================================================
- No durable store of ANY kind: no proof store, readiness artifact, finding
  registry, campaign-rule store, second audit database, no file emission.
- No production ranker, embedding model, vector database, or graph database.
- No universal relationship vocabulary, clause ontology, or obligation identity.
- No claim of universal discovery completeness anywhere in code or comments.
- No campaign-rule/ruling schema, storage, resolver, or lifecycle: those are
  `eshyra-jhpt`'s. Discovery may not resolve an ambiguity.
- No runtime integration: the orchestrator seam is W9. Nothing in the existing
  runtime may import the discovery modules.
- Do not weaken the W7 fixtures, `diagnosticFixtureCorpus.test.ts`, or any
  existing audit expectation to make a probe pass.

====================================================================
J. WORKFLOW
